t:
(a) 
Section 4107(c)(3) is amended by striking out “section 4507” and inserting in lieu thereof “sections 4507 and 5384”.
 
    (b) Section 4109(b) is amended—

        (1) 
by inserting “after August 25, 1980,” after “any period of service”; and
 
        (2) 
by inserting “after such date” after “such service”.

fable.w: This section only makes technical conforming amendments, swapping cross-references and inserting date qualifiers into existing provisions. There is no tempting reading here: it mentions no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.

opus.w: The section only makes technical changes: it updates a cross-reference and adds a date limit to existing provisions. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking authority, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. Amending a statute is not, by itself, a process that brings outsiders into a federal decision.
opus.b: **Tempting reading:** Someone might call this participation because it amends statutory provisions, and amendments can sometimes involve rulemaking or outside processes. That reading fails here. The text only swaps cross-references ("section 4507" becomes "sections 4507 and 5384") and adds a date limit ("after August 25, 1980"). No one outside the federal government is involved.

qwen_chat.w: This section contains only textual amendments to existing statutes (Section 4107 and Section 4109). It does not create any advisory bodies, comment periods, hearings, or consultation requirements with non-federal entities. The changes are limited to updating cross-references and dates within the statutory text.

Temptation: Nothing. The text is purely technical amendments to other sections of the law, changing dates and cross-references. It does not establish any process for outside parties to participate in decision-making.
Resolution: This section contains only textual amendments to existing statutes (Section 4107 and Section 4109). It does not create any advisory bodies, comment periods, hearings, or consultation requirements with non-federal entities.
